record.original_question: Chandee and Soundararajan proved, under the Riemann Hypothesis, that |zeta(1/2 + it)| is bounded by exp((C0 + o(1)) log t / log log t) with C0 = (log 2)/2. Reduce the constant C0 in this bound.

evidence.quote: Chandee and Soundararajan [15] proved that the Riemann Hypothesis implies |ζ(1/2 + it)| << exp((C0 + o(1)) log t / log log t) with C0 = log 2 / 2 = 0.1505 ... . Reduce the value of C0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\zeta(s)$ denote the Riemann zeta function. Assume the Riemann Hypothesis (i.e., that all non-trivial zeros of $\zeta$ have real part $1/2$). It is known that under this assumption,
$$|\zeta(\tfrac12 + it)| \ll \exp\!\left( (C_0 + o(1)) \, \frac{\log t}{\log\log t} \right) \qquad (t \to \infty),$$
holds with the constant $C_0 = \tfrac{\log 2}{2}$. 

Problem: Establish such a bound with a strictly smaller admissible constant $C_0 < \tfrac{\log 2}{2}$, i.e., reduce the value of $C_0$ in the above pointwise estimate for $|\zeta(1/2+it)|$ on the Riemann Hypothesis.
artifact.status_search_result: The Chandee–Soundararajan bound with constant $C_0 = (\log 2)/2$, established in 2009, remains the best known pointwise upper bound for $|\zeta(1/2+it)|$ under RH. Subsequent work (e.g., Carneiro–Chandee, Chirre–Gonçalves–de Laat, and explicit refinements) has improved implied constants and explicit versions but has not lowered the leading constant $(\log 2)/2$ in the asymptotic exponent. No published reduction of $C_0$ has been verified.

status_evidence.title: Bounding |ζ(1/2 + it)| on the Riemann hypothesis
status_evidence.snippet: Chandee and Soundararajan show that on RH, any C > (log 2)/2 is admissible in Littlewood's bound |ζ(1/2+it)| ≪ exp(C log t/log log t).
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the current best constant C_0 = (log 2)/2 in the conditional pointwise bound.

status_evidence.title: On explicit estimates for S(t), S1(t), and ζ(1/2+it) under the Riemann Hypothesis
status_evidence.snippet: Provides explicit refinements of conditional bounds for ζ(1/2+it) under RH but retains the same leading constant.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work refines lower-order terms but does not reduce the constant (log 2)/2.
